title: Where Spark raises beyond the reference, and where it errors without an error class
verdict: extra raises: `INT` positions, ANSI string casts, `element_at(…, 0)`, regexes, week patterns; bare Java exceptions (SP-3, SP-4)
description: Under ANSI Spark raises where the reference computes in these places: a `substring` position or length from 2³¹ to 2³² (`CAST_OVERFLOW`, spark-substring-range); an implicit cast of a string in arithmetic or a comparison (`1 + '1.5'`, `1 = '1.0'`: `CAST_INVALID_INPUT`, spark-implicit-casts); `a[i]` out of range. In both modes: `element_at(a, 0)`, an invalid regex or group index, `date_format` week letters, `ntile(0)`, a `DECIMAL(39,…)` type, and `-x` of a 38-digit decimal (SP-1).

Most errors carry an error class and SQLSTATE. Two do not: timestamp arithmetic past the microsecond range raises `java.lang.ArithmeticException: long overflow` (SP-3), and an invalid constant regex on the codegen path raises `java.util.regex.PatternSyntaxException` (SP-4). Two more raise without a class in both modes: `to_timestamp('294248', 'y')`, a year past the microsecond range, raises `java.lang.ArithmeticException: long overflow` (SP-6), and `TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(0.1234567)`, a decimal with more than six fractional digits, raises `java.lang.ArithmeticException: Rounding necessary` (SP-7), where a double truncates to microseconds. Planning errors (`DATATYPE_MISMATCH`, `UNSUPPORTED_TIME_TYPE`) come when the query is analysed, before any row is read.
Silent wrong results, the opposite case: `date_add` wraps (SP-2), decimal negation rounds (SP-1), `floor(NaN)` is 0 under ANSI (SP-5).
reference: The reference raises only where its options say (D2); an engine's extra raises are allowed where they happen only on rows the reference would also reject, and otherwise make a plan that verifies fail at run time. A writer avoids each listed form or guards it.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: the same raises with ANSI off
the same is NULL with ANSI off
`regexp_extract(…, 3)` with two groups raises `INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE.REGEX_GROUP_INDEX`, ANSI on
`to_timestamp('294248', 'y')` raises a bare `java.lang.ArithmeticException: long overflow`, no error class, ANSI on
`TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(0.1234567)` (a decimal) raises a bare `java.lang.ArithmeticException: Rounding necessary`, ANSI on

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

evidence.note: `extractMicros` turns the parsed date-time into microseconds with `Math.multiplyExact`, which throws `ArithmeticException: long overflow` past the range
under ANSI, `parseToTimestampExact` wraps only `DateTimeException` and `ParseException` in an error class; the `ArithmeticException` propagates
without ANSI, `isParseError` turns only the same parse errors into NULL, so the overflow raises there too
`decimalToMicros` calls `longValueExact()` on seconds × 10⁶ and rethrows a bare `ArithmeticException` unless the value is outside the long range
the codegen path does the same: `throw e`
raise_set[0], substring_range[0], list_index[0], decimal_negate[0], round[0], date_range[1]

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 25384 of 25384 results as the fact says; Spark's value differs from Rel.eval's (sverify's lift, reference profile) on 435 of 1754 rows compared.

It exercises the raising rows: substring positions past 32 bits, element_at at 0 and out of range, a 38-digit decimal negated, floor of ±inf, timestamps past the microsecond range, and `n + s` with a string.

raise_set[0]: 300 rows, `n + s`, `element_at(a, i)`, 1812 of 1812 results as the fact says (raised: CAST_INVALID_INPUT 30, INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX_IN_ELEMENT_AT 21, INVALID_INDEX_OF_ZERO 39); substring_range[0]: 300 rows, `substring(s, p, l)`, 794 of 794 results as the fact says (raised: CAST_OVERFLOW 30); list_index[0]: 300 rows, `element_at(a, i)`, `a[i]`, `get(a, i)`, `try_element_at(a, i)`, `size(a)`, `array_size(a)`, 6326 of 6326 results as the fact says (raised: INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX 30, INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX_IN_ELEMENT_AT 28, INVALID_INDEX_OF_ZERO 92); decimal_negate[0]: 300 rows, `-x`, `abs(x)`, `0 - x`, 3536 of 3536 results as the fact says (raised: NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE.WITHOUT_SUGGESTION 120); Spark differs from Rel.eval on 394 of 554; round[0]: 300 rows, `round(x, 0)`, `bround(x, 0)`, `round(x, 1)`, `bround(x, 1)`, `round(x, 2)`, `bround(x, 2)`, `round(x, -2)`, `bround(x, -2)`, `floor(x)`, `ceil(x)`, 11956 of 11956 results as the fact says (raised: ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW 60); Spark differs from Rel.eval on 41 of 1200; date_range[1]: 300 rows, `unix_micros(CAST(timestamp_micros(us) AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ) + make_dt_interval(n, 0, 0, 0))`, 960 of 960 results as the fact says (raised: java.lang.ArithmeticException 60).
Spark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.12.1, Linux amd64, local[2], session time zone UTC.
